title: Why Scheduling is Hard
subtitle: The mathematics behind your school timetable
intro: Creating a school timetable looks simple, but it's actually one of the most computationally difficult problems in mathematics.

searchSpace.title: The Search Space
searchSpace.explanation: Each lesson needs a time slot and a room. This creates an astronomical number of possible combinations:
searchSpace.note: This is a simplified calculation. Real scheduling has dependencies that make it even harder.

atoms.title: Atoms in the Universe
atoms.comparison: Our search space is larger than the number of atoms in the observable universe.

chess.title: Chess Games Ever Played
chess.comparison: More possibilities than every chess game ever played, combined.

sudoku.title: Sudoku Puzzles
sudoku.comparison: Equivalent to billions of billions of Sudoku puzzles.

bruteForce.title: Brute Force Time
bruteForce.comparison: Even checking one billion schedules per second would take longer than the age of the universe.

whySolver.title: Why Use a Solver?
whySolver.explanation: Instead of trying every combination, which is impossible, the solver uses:

constructionHeuristic.name: Construction Heuristic
constructionHeuristic.description: Builds a good initial solution using placement strategies

localSearch.name: Local Search
localSearch.description: Iteratively improves the solution by making targeted changes

constraintPropagation.name: Constraint Propagation
constraintPropagation.description: Eliminates impossible choices early to reduce the search space

whySolver.result: The solver finds a good solution in minutes, not millennia.

constraints.title: The Rules Make It Harder
constraints.explanation: Each constraint reduces the valid solutions, making the problem even more constrained:

animation.description: As we add more lessons, the possibilities explode exponentially:

footer.appreciation: Next time you see your schedule, remember it is the result of algorithms tackling one of computing's hardest problems.
